pain_point: Free web PDF tools upload sensitive files to unknown servers, watermark output, cap daily use and push subscriptions, so people hesitate to merge/compress/sign contracts, IDs and statements.
segment: Freelancers, small-business owners, job applicants, renters and students who handle sensitive PDFs occasionally
micro_app_idea: A local-only (nothing uploaded) PDF toolkit: merge, split, reorder, rotate, compress and redact, sold once and usable offline.

evidence.what: Maker thread lists three hates about free PDF tools: 'They upload your files to their servers (not great for contracts, IDs, statements)', watermarked outputs, and daily caps that lead to subscription prompts (seen via search excerpt; page not opened).
Post titled 'Tired of $288/year PDF subscriptions? Try $19 forever, zero uploads'; describes a $19 single-payment browser tool for merge/split/compress that works offline (search excerpt).
Sponsored deal copy: 'Uploading a signed contract or a client invoice to some random cloud-based PDF tool always feels a little risky'; offline editor at one-time $39.99 vs $99.99 list.
Forum user reports paying $99 for PDF Candy Pro, key then stopped working after reinstall; another commenter says client-side online editors give 'the same level of privacy as a desktop tool'.

paid_alternatives.name: IndyPDF lifetime (deal price vs $49.99 list; URL attribution inferred from article title about a ~$20 offline lifetime PDF editor)

queries: offline pdf editor one time purchase

urgency_basis: Recurring, widely shared annoyance (privacy + caps + watermarks) but rarely a crisis; tone is 'feels risky/annoying', not 'losing money'.
wtp_20_evidence: Competitors already sell one-time offline PDF editors at $19.99-$39.99 and a $19 one-time tool is marketed against a $288/year subscription, so $20 sits at the low end of proven price points.
risks: Highly saturated (free client-side tools exist); 'no upload' claim must be verifiable; refund/licence-key friction is a reported complaint; user-reported anecdotes only. Buildability note: Merge/split/rotate/sign are feasible client-side; high-quality compression and OCR are harder.

Vendor page states HEIC to JPG limits: 1 conversion/day anonymous, 15/day signed in, 150/day premium; 100-file batches only on premium.

Comparison table (single article) lists per-batch caps such as 30 files (iLoveIMG), 10 (Convertio), 5 (FreeConvert) and 25/day (CloudConvert); macOS Preview and some desktop tools listed as unlimited.
Convertio reviewers complain of download errors and a paywall that appears only when pressing download; one cites about EUR9/month.

paid_alternatives.name: Wallpapers.com HEIC converter premium (price not seen)

queries: convert heic to jpg bulk no limit

urgency_basis: Complaints about unexpected recurring charges are angry in tone, but the underlying need is occasional and free offline options (macOS Preview, free desktop tools) exist.

risks: Free built-ins (macOS Preview, Windows HEIC extension) cover the HEIC case; Windows HEVC extension friction; review evidence is self-selected; low differentiation unless it bundles many formats. Buildability note: Fully local image conversion; no proprietary data or compliance.

pain_point: Resume builders advertise cheap trials/one-time downloads, then bill every ~4 weeks and make cancelling or refunds hard.
segment: Job seekers (entry-level to mid-career) who need a clean ATS-friendly resume and a quick tailoring pass per application
micro_app_idea: A local resume builder with ATS-safe templates, PDF/DOCX export and a rule-based keyword-gap check against a pasted job posting; pay once, no account.

evidence.what: Reviewer says a $23 charge hit every four weeks (not monthly) with no billing email; another says a failed cancellation after trial led to months of charges and refund refusal (unverified complaints).
Reviewers describe a $2.95 trial followed by a $29.95 charge, and a trial turning into EUR21.95 every four weeks; Trustpilot summary flags surprise renewals and hard cancellations.

urgency_basis: Job-search stress plus angry billing complaints across multiple sites; need is episodic but time-boxed and high stakes.
wtp_20_evidence: Incumbents charge about $23-$30 per billing cycle (repeating every ~4 weeks per reviewers), so a single $20 payment is cheaper than one cycle.
risks: Extremely saturated and SEO-dominated; free builders exist; complaint data is self-selected; keyword-matching claims should not promise interviews (one source notes 'tailoring doesn't guarantee interviews'). Buildability note: Template rendering plus literal keyword matching is straightforward; no AI required for MVP.

pain_point: People sharing photos online or with buyers want to strip GPS and camera metadata in bulk, but web tools handle one file at a time and miss sidecar data.
segment: Marketplace sellers, parents, realtors and creators sharing photos publicly
micro_app_idea: Offline batch EXIF/GPS stripper with a before/after report of what metadata was found and selective keep options (e.g. keep camera settings, drop GPS).

evidence.what: ExifStrip iOS: free with in-app purchases, up to 50 photos per batch, works offline, share-sheet extension.
Guide notes the browser remover does not batch whole folders and does not detect Lightroom edit data stored in separate XMP files.
Free-to-try browser stripper; paid tier lets you choose which fields to keep, e.g., strip GPS but keep camera settings.

paid_alternatives.name: Wallpapers.com EXIF Stripper paid tier (price not seen)

queries: strip gps from photos before sharing

urgency_basis: Privacy-aware but low-urgency; no complaint threads found, only tool listings.
risks: Free command-line (ExifTool) and many free web tools exist; no WTP evidence; evidence is vendor listings only. Buildability note: Local metadata parsing/removal is simple; XMP sidecar support adds a little.

pain_point: Videos exceed chat/email upload limits (Discord free reportedly lowered to 10 MB; Gmail counts attachments up to 25 MB) and trimming/compressing is fiddly.
segment: Casual users, gamers, remote workers sharing screen clips
micro_app_idea: Pick a target size (10 MB / 25 MB), auto-trim and compress to hit it with one click, offline.

evidence.what: Sept 2024 report that Discord's support page announced lowering the free-user file limit to 10 MB (previously 25 MB).
Feb 2026 guide still says free users can only upload files up to 25 MB, so sources disagree on the current cap.
Free browser tool 'Under 10 MB - No upload' for Discord, showing competition is free.

urgency_basis: Frequent minor annoyance but multiple free tools solve it.
risks: Free competitors abundant; platform limits change; no WTP evidence. Buildability note: ffmpeg.wasm/ffmpeg wrapper with target-size presets is feasible.

pain_point: Loom's free plan limits recordings to 25 videos and 5 minutes, pushing users to $12.50-$18/creator/month plans.
segment: Solo workers, teachers, support staff making quick screen walkthroughs
micro_app_idea: Local screen+mic recorder with trimming and instant MP4 export, no time or count caps and no cloud; one-time purchase.

evidence.what: Loom free plan: 25 videos per person, 5-minute recordings, 720p; delete or upgrade after 25.
Loom pricing page review: paid plans billed annually; per-creator monthly costs differ by source ($12.50, $15, $18).
Movavi lifetime licence for one PC listed at $74.95 (page titled 2023, may be outdated).

paid_alternatives.name: Movavi Screen Recorder lifetime (1 PC, 2023 page)

urgency_basis: Limit-driven annoyance; OBS and OS built-in recorders are free.
wtp_20_evidence: Lifetime recorders are listed at $39.99-$74.95 and Loom costs $12.50+/month, so $20 undercuts comparables, though free OBS competes.
risks: OBS and OS-level recorders are free; Loom's value is sharing links (needs hosting); heavily crowded. Buildability note: Browser getDisplayMedia/MediaRecorder or Electron is feasible; polish and trimming take effort.

pain_point: Photographers and sellers need quick batch resize + watermark + export presets for client delivery without paying a creative-cloud subscription.
segment: Hobbyist photographers, small studios and online sellers
micro_app_idea: Drag a folder, apply saved resize/watermark/sharpen presets, and export web and proof versions in one pass.

evidence.what: PhotoBatcher Pro Mac app at $6.99 resizes, watermarks, crops and bulk-exports.
Resize & Watermark Pro (Photoshop script) at $4.99+ one-time; no recurring fees; sales final.
Adobe community thread titled 'price increase unacceptable' about Lightroom/Photography plan pricing.

urgency_basis: Workflow convenience; Lightroom already supports export presets and watermarks.
risks: Comparable tools sell at $4.99-$6.99 so $20 is above market anchors; Lightroom covers it for subscribers; commodity feature set. Buildability note: Local image processing only.

pain_point: Exporting a long AI chat to Word/PDF without losing tables, code blocks, headings and formulas is clumsy; browser print includes site chrome.
segment: Students, consultants and analysts reusing AI-assisted research in documents
micro_app_idea: Local tool that turns a saved/exported chat file into a clean, styled DOCX/PDF with tables and code preserved.

evidence.what: Forum request to convert a long ChatGPT chat to Word/PDF without losing headings, tables, code blocks, images or formulas; one user says Chrome print-to-PDF works but captures the website interface.
Free Chrome extension covering PDF, Word, Google Docs and Notion export.
'ChatGPT Share to PDF' extension claims local processing and preserved code blocks/tables.

queries: save chatgpt chat as pdf with tables

urgency_basis: Low-urgency convenience; many free extensions.
risks: Free extensions dominate; OpenAI/other vendors may add native export (not verified); platform terms and DOM changes; no WTP evidence. Buildability note: Formatting conversion is easy; browser-extension DOM scraping breaks when UIs change.

pain_point: Etsy sellers spend 20-40 minutes per listing on titles, descriptions and the 13 tags, and keyword tools are subscriptions.
segment: Small Etsy sellers (handmade, print-on-demand, digital downloads)
micro_app_idea: Offline tag/title builder that expands a seed phrase into buyer-language variants, checks character limits and fills all 13 tags; one-time price.

evidence.what: Seller-tool vendor blog: unused tag slots reduce visibility; shoppers search 'gift for dad' not technical terms; listing copy takes 20-40 minutes per listing (vendor estimate, unverified).
Marmalead lists a lifetime plan at $300 (per search excerpt), showing sellers will pay for keyword tools.
etsys.in offers 11 free tools with no signup, evidence of free competition.

urgency_basis: Time-saver for sellers; evidence is vendor claims, not seller complaints.
wtp_20_evidence: Marmalead's $300 lifetime plan shows sellers pay for keyword data, but a data-less $20 tool is a weaker offer.
risks: Etsy platform and policy changes; no proprietary keyword data; free tools abound; evidence is vendor-sourced. Buildability note: Without live search-volume data the tool is only a formatter/idea expander; real keyword data requires a data source.
